evidence.description: FIND-002 confirmed RESOLVED by direct Read: makeRouteCache is imported and wired into directionsMinutes via cache.getOrCompute("_shared", srcGeo, dstGeo, timeBucket(departAtMs), compute), and travel-transit-wire.test.js's 'repeated ticks... call the provider ONCE' test exercises this exact path. scheduler.js:15,115-116 passes directionsMinutes as wake-filter.js's resolveDeparture's directionsFn, so the live 60s scheduler tick benefits from the same cache — confirmed a REAL production caller, not just a test.

FIND-006 confirmed RESOLVED: grep for require(.*money-path shows real production importers (money-path-smoke.mjs, money-path-monitor.mjs) in addition to money-path.test.js; grep for require(.*route-cache shows travel.js as a real production importer in addition to its tests. No dead-but-tested modules remain.

Synth-failure fallback verified safe: playWakeClip's catch calls openGeminiLive() (never leaves the call silent); openGeminiLive is idempotent via `if (gemini) return;` and is called from exactly two sites (DTMF interaction, synth-failure catch) with JS's single-threaded event loop precluding a double-open race — hand-traced, matches iteration-3's already-PASSED finding on this exact code path (unchanged in this iteration).

FIND-006 resolved: both modules now have real, non-test production importers (grep confirmed) — no drift between tested-but-dead logic and weaker hand-rolled reimplementations. No new duplication introduced by this iteration's changes; nixpacks.toml/voice-synth.cjs/transit.js/travel.js/money-path-monitor.mjs are each focused, single-responsibility files consistent with the pre-existing module boundaries.

FIND-001 config-level fix verified plausible: [phases.setup] nixPkgs=["...", "ffmpeg", "python313Packages.edge-tts"] follows the documented nixpacks.toml pattern ("..." preserves auto-detected packages) and both listed nix packages are real. This cannot be proven against the live Railway host from disk alone — flagged as a REQUIRED POST-MERGE VERIFICATION (re-run the real-call E2E against the deployed Railway URL), not a blocker, per the synth-failure fallback already being proven safe (never-silent) independent of whether ffmpeg/edge-tts are actually present.

FIND-001.note: nixpacks.toml config is syntactically correct and adds the right packages; synth-failure fallback (server.js:401-405) is proven safe (escalates to Live, never silent) independent of whether the config actually works on Railway. No blocker remains on disk, but PROD PROOF (re-run the real-call E2E against the deployed Railway URL, confirm live_ws_opened=0) is still outstanding and required before this can be called fully closed.

FIND-002.note: route-cache.js wired into travel.js's directionsMinutes via cache.getOrCompute; scheduler.js → wake-filter.js's resolveDeparture → directionsMinutes is a confirmed real production call path; travel-transit-wire.test.js proves 1-call-per-(geo,bucket) across repeated ticks.

FIND-003.note: netlify-deploy.yml's post-restore reverification (real flap guard) is correctly implemented. The standalone 15-min monitor (money-path-monitor.mjs) exists and reuses RollbackController/assertMoneyPath, but its OWN flap-guard input (lastGoodPasses) is derived from deploy-existence, not deploy-health (FIND-102), and its state-file read is unguarded against corruption (FIND-103) — the continuous-monitoring half of C6/Goal-5 is not yet trustworthy.

FIND-004.note: parseTransitPlan now adds walk time into durationSecs (no longer silently drops it), but the added formula double-counts egressWalkSecs — proven from the fixture's own numbers and baked into transit.test.js's assertion (FIND-101). The direction of the resulting error is conservative (over-, not under-, estimate) so it does not violate the never-late invariant, but the claim 'FIXED + verified' in execution-notes.md is not accurate as written.

FIND-005.note: Accepted deviation, as documented by the builder: geocodeAddress memoizes on the module-level _geoMemo Map (travel.js:155,161), so repeated 60s ticks do not re-hit the Geocoding API for the same address. In-process (not DB-persisted) is a reasonable tradeoff for the stated cost goal; this is a judgment call, not a correctness defect.

FIND-006.note: grep-confirmed real production importers for both previously-dead modules: money-path.js ← money-path-smoke.mjs + money-path-monitor.mjs; route-cache.js ← travel.js.

findings.issue: parseTransitPlan double-counts egressWalkSecs: best.durationSecs from the transit.ls8h.com API already includes the egress walk (proven from the committed fixture's own numbers: journey.arrivalSecs - leg.arrivalSecs == egressWalkSecs in every journey), but the FIND-004 fix adds accessWalkSecs+egressWalkSecs on top of it, over-counting egress by one full egressWalkSecs. transit.test.js:29 now asserts the incorrect value (1219) as correct, so the test enforces the bug.
findings.fix: durationSecs should be best.durationSecs + accessWalkSecs only (no re-add of egressWalkSecs); update the fixture-derived test expectation to 1090.

findings.issue: The 15-min monitor's flap-guard input (lastGoodPasses) is Boolean(prev.id) — 'a prior deploy exists' — not an actual assertMoneyPath check on that deploy's content, unlike netlify-deploy.yml's real post-restore reverification. Two consecutive bad deploys would cause the monitor to roll back into another bad deploy without escalating, defeating RollbackController's own documented flap-guard invariant.
findings.fix: Fetch and assertMoneyPath the candidate rollback target's actual content before setting lastGoodPasses, mirroring netlify-deploy.yml's approach.

findings.issue: JSON.parse(readFileSync(STATE)) has no try/catch. A corrupted/partial .monitor-state.json (crash mid-write, no lockfile against concurrent runs) permanently crashes every future run of the ONE continuous safety net this feature adds, with zero test coverage for money-path-monitor.mjs's own integration logic.
findings.fix: Wrap the state read in try/catch, fall back to fresh RollbackController defaults on parse failure, and add a test for the corrupted-state case.
